topics.topic: At kernel start/check_installed_instances, who enforces credential-header collision with kernel-set headers and what refusal outcome is returned
questions: At start, who enforces A09 rule 1's other refusal case: credential header collides with a header the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, `content-length`), and what exact refusal outcome is returned?
Which module/step performs the credential-header-vs-kernel-set-header start check, and what exact refusal outcome is returned when it fails?

quotes: The start check that no credential header has the name of a required header (A09 rule 1) is `bindings.check_installed_instances`, a required start step that `surface` calls right after `installation.load_installation` and before the store is opened; it reads only the installation and the manifest, never the store.
an installation whose credential header has, compared without regard to case, the name of a required header, or of a header the kernel sets itself (A08 rule 5), refuses to start.
judgement.why: The texts already specify both the enforcing module/step and that this condition causes start refusal.

topics.topic: After owner approval, whether a request mismatch (with no standing grant) requires obtaining a new approval before sending
questions: After the owner approves, if the rebuilt request no longer matches that approval and no standing grant applies, must this approve call still send, or must it create/wait for a new approval?

topics.topic: In propose/accept recheck, whether required-header collisions with kernel-set headers are rejected as manifest mismatch or deferred to send-time checks
questions: During propose/accept recheck, is a required header name that collides (case-insensitively) with a kernel-set header refused here as `manifest mismatch` (as A08 rule 5 states), or is it left to send-time checks only?
